label: def:almost_surely
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:almost_surely}
Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote probability, and let $x$ be a random variable.
 
A property of $x$ is said to hold \textit{almost surely} if it holds with probability one under $\mathbb{P}$.
 
Equivalently, the property holds for every value $x$ can take except possibly for a set of values whose total probability is zero, and such exceptional values can therefore be disregarded in practice.
 
Equivalently, the set of values of $x$ for which the property fails has measure zero.
 
For example, if $x$ is uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$, then $x\neq0.5$ holds almost surely, since the single value $x=0.5$ has probability zero, even though $x=0.5$ remains a possible outcome.

title: Proof
body_md:
It follows from \eqref{eq:fisher_information} that
${\mathcal F}_{k+1}-{\mathcal F}_k=\phi_k\phi_k^{\rm T} \succeq 0$, since $\phi_k\phi_k^{\rm T}$ is positive semidefinite for every $\phi_k$.
 
Monotonicity of $\lambda_{\min}(\cdot)$ under the Loewner order then implies that $\lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_{k+1})\geq\lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_k)$.

label: prop:multisine_rank
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:multisine_rank}
Consider the system \eqref{eq:system} with regressor
$\phi_k\in{\mathbb R}^{2n}$ defined by \eqref{eq:regression}.
Assume that $G(q)$ is driven by the multisine input \eqref{eq:multisine_input}.
                                                   
Let $H\in{\mathbb R}^{2n\times 2n}$ satisfy
\eqref{eq:regressor_sinusoidal_mapping}.
If
$$
\operatorname{rank} H = 2n,
$$
then the steady-state regressor sequence $\{\phi_k\}$ is persistently
exciting.

label: prop:whitenoise_rank
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:whitenoise_rank}
Consider the system \eqref{eq:system} with regressor $\phi_k\in{\mathbb R}^{2n}$ defined by \eqref{eq:regression}.
  
Let $\{u_k\}$ be a zero-mean white-noise sequence satisfying
$$
\mathbb E[u_k^2]
    =
    \sigma_u^2
    >
    0.
$$
Assume that the corresponding steady-state regressor covariance satisfies
$$
R_\phi
    \stackrel{\triangle}{=}
    \mathbb E
    \left[
        \phi_k\phi_k^{\rm T}
    \right]
    >
    0.
$$
Then, the regressor sequence $\{\phi_k\}$ is persistently exciting in expectation.
  
In particular, there exist an integer $N>0$ and a scalar $\alpha>0$ such that
\begin{align}
    \mathbb E
    \left[
        \sum_{i=k}^{k+N-1}
            \phi_i\phi_i^{\rm T}
    \right]
        &\geq
        \alpha I_{2n}
\end{align}
for all $k.$

label: thm:self_regulating
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:self_regulating}
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:information_bound}, almost surely,
\begin{align}
    \sigma_k
        &\rightarrow
        0,
    \\
    p_k
        &\rightarrow
        0,
    \\
    \lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_k)
        &\rightarrow
        \infty,
    \\
    \hat\theta_k
        &\rightarrow
        \theta,
    \\
    \frac{\sigma_k}{p_k}
        &\rightarrow
        \infty.
\end{align}
head: environment

title: Proof

label: rem:beta_effect
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:beta_effect}
Simulations over the tested range of $\beta$ indicate that $p_k={\mathcal O}(k^{-\gamma})$, where the rate $\gamma$ decreases monotonically as $\beta$ increases.
 
A larger $\beta$ gives a smaller $\sigma_k$ for the same $p_k$, so less excitation is injected and $p_k$ decays more slowly.
 
The exponent $\beta$ therefore trades the rate of covariance decay against the amount of excitation retained.
 
A rigorous characterization of $\gamma$ as a function of $\beta$ is left to future work.
head: environment

label: ex:three_case
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:three_case}
\textup{Effect of self-regulating excitation on persistent excitation and parameter convergence.}
Consider the third-order system
\begin{align}
    y_k
        &=
        \frac{0.5 q^2 - 0.2 q + 0.1}{q^3 - 0.8 q^2 - 0.03 q + 0.09}
        u_k,
\end{align}
with poles at $0.5$, $0.6$, and $-0.3$.
 
Define $\phi_k\stackrel{\triangle}{=}[-y_{k-1}\ -y_{k-2}\ -y_{k-3}\ u_{k-1}\ u_{k-2}\ u_{k-3}]^{\rm T}$, so that $y_k=\phi_k^{\rm T}\theta$ with $\theta=[-0.8\ -0.03\ 0.09\ 0.5\ -0.2\ 0.1]^{\rm T}$.
 
To apply RLS, let $P_0=10I_6$ and $\hat\theta_0=0$.
 
Consider the plant input defined in \eqref{eq:nominal_plus_white_noise}, with the nominal input
\begin{align}
\bar u_k
&=
\sin(0.3k)+\sin(0.75k+0.4),
\end{align}
which is a two-tone multisine input.
 
Since $\phi_k\in{\mathbb R}^6$ requires three distinct frequencies for $H$ in \eqref{eq:regressor_sinusoidal_mapping} to have full rank, the two-tone input $\bar u_k$ alone is not persistently exciting.

Three choices of $\sigma_k$ are considered: $\sigma_k=0$ (Case 1); $\sigma_k=0.5$, constant (Case 2); and $\sigma_k$ self-regulating per \eqref{eq:self_regulating_sigma} with $\sigma_0=0.5$, $\beta=0.8$ (Case 3).
 
Figure~\ref{fig:three_case} shows, for all three cases, the parameter error $\|\theta_k-\theta\|$, the covariance measure $\lambda_{\max}(P_k)$, the Fisher information measure $\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal F_k)$, and the excitation amplitude $\sigma_k$.

 
In Case 1, the parameter error does not converge to zero, $\lambda_{\max}(P_k)$ plateaus, and $\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal F_k)$ plateaus rather than growing without bound, confirming the lack of persistent excitation identified above.

 
In Cases 2 and 3, the injected noise restores persistent excitation: the parameter error and $\lambda_{\max}(P_k)$ converge to zero, and $\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal F_k)$ grows without bound, consistent with Theorem~\ref{thm:self_regulating}.
 
However, $\sigma_k$ remains constant in Case 2, whereas $\sigma_k$ vanishes in Case 3, confirming the remaining claim of Theorem~\ref{thm:self_regulating}.
\hfill$\Diamond$
head: environment

label: ex:beta_sweep
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:beta_sweep}
\textup{Effect of $\beta$ on the rate of covariance decay.}
Reconsider Example~\ref{ex:three_case} with $\sigma_k$ given by \eqref{eq:self_regulating_sigma} for
$$
\beta\in\{0,\,0.01,\,0.1,\,0.3,\,0.5,\,0.7,\,0.9,\,1.2,\,1.8\}.
$$
Figure~\ref{fig:beta_sweep} shows, for each value of $\beta$, $\lambda_{\max}(P_k)$, $\sigma_k$, and the ratio $\sigma_k/\lambda_{\max}(P_k)$, together with the exponent $\gamma$ obtained by fitting a line to $\log\lambda_{\max}(P_k)$ versus $\log k$ over the final $70\%$ of the run.
 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
For $\beta<1$ in this sweep, $\sigma_k/\lambda_{\max}(P_k)\rightarrow\infty$, confirming the claim of Theorem~\ref{thm:self_regulating}.
 
For $\beta=1.2$ and $\beta=1.8$, which fall outside the hypothesis $0<\beta<1$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:self_regulating}, $\sigma_k/\lambda_{\max}(P_k)\rightarrow0$ instead, since $\sigma_k/p_k=(\sigma_0/p_0^\beta)p_k^{\beta-1}$ and $\beta-1>0$ reverses the sign of the limiting exponent as $p_k\rightarrow0$.
 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
The fitted rate $\gamma$ decreases monotonically as $\beta$ increases, confirming Remark~\ref{rem:beta_effect}.
 
Smaller $\beta$ yields faster covariance decay at the cost of more persistent excitation, larger $\beta$ yields the reverse, and no intermediate value of $\beta$ improves both simultaneously.
\hfill$\Diamond$

title: Proof
body_md:
By linearity of $G(q)$, $\phi_k=\bar\phi_k+\sigma\phi_k^w$, where $\bar\phi_k$ is generated by $\bar u_k$ and is deterministic.
 
Since $\phi_k^w$ is zero mean,
\begin{align}
    \mathbb E[\phi_k\phi_k^{\rm T}]
        &=
        \bar\phi_k\bar\phi_k^{\rm T}
        +
        \sigma^2R_w
        \succeq
        \sigma^2R_w.
    \nonumber
\end{align}
 
Summing over $i=k,\ldots,k+N-1$ and using $R_w\succeq\lambda_{\min}(R_w)I_{2n}$ gives (a).

By definition of ${\mathcal F}_k^w$ and stationarity of $\phi_k^w$, $\mathbb E[{\mathcal F}_k^w]=k\sigma^2R_w$.
 
Since $\lambda_{\min}(A+B)\geq\lambda_{\min}(A)+\lambda_{\min}(B)$ for symmetric $A$ and $B$,
\begin{align}
    \lambda_{\max}(\bar P_k)
        &=
        \frac{1}{\lambda_{\min}\left(P_0^{-1}+k\sigma^2R_w\right)}
        \nonumber \\
        &
        \leq
        \frac{1}{\lambda_{\min}(P_0^{-1})+k\sigma^2\lambda_{\min}(R_w)},
    \nonumber
\end{align}
which gives (b).

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $p_k$ is nonincreasing, $\sigma_k\leq\sigma_0$.
 
Stability of $G(q)$ and boundedness of $\bar u_k$, $\sigma_k$, and $w_k$ give $\|\phi_k\|^2\leq B$.

Fix $k\geq1$ and $k\leq l\leq k+N-1$.
 
Then $P_l^{-1}\preceq P_{k-1}^{-1}+NB\,I_{2n}\preceq(1+NBp_0)P_{k-1}^{-1}$, so $p_l\geq p_{k-1}/(1+NBp_0)$ and, by \eqref{eq:self_regulating_sigma},
\begin{align}
    \sigma_l
        &\geq
        \rho\,\sigma_{k-1},
    \qquad
    \rho
        \stackrel{\triangle}{=}
        (1+NBp_0)^{-\beta}.
    \nonumber
\end{align}

For a unit vector $v$ and $k\leq i\leq k+N-1$, linearity of $G(q)$ gives
\begin{align}
    v^{\rm T}\phi_i
        &=
        m_i
        +
        \sum_{l=k}^{i-1}
            c_{i-l}(v)\,\sigma_l w_l,
    \nonumber
\end{align}
where $m_i$ is computable from ${\mathcal H}_{k-1}$ and $c_d(v)$ are fixed coefficients determined by $v$ and the impulse response of $G(q)$.
 
Since $\sigma_l$ is computable from ${\mathcal H}_{l-1}$ and $w_l$ is independent of ${\mathcal H}_{l-1}$ with zero mean and unit variance, the cross terms vanish under ${\mathbb E}[\cdot\mid{\mathcal H}_{k-1}]$, and
\begin{align}
    v^{\rm T}
    {\mathbb E}\left[{\mathcal F}_{k+N}-{\mathcal F}_k\mid{\mathcal H}_{k-1}\right]
    v
        &\geq
        \rho^2\sigma_{k-1}^2\sum_{d=1}^{N-1}(N-d)\,c_d(v)^2.
    \nonumber
\end{align}

For minimal $G(q)$ and $N=2n+1$, no unit $v$ has $c_1(v)=\cdots=c_{2n}(v)=0$, since this would give a pole-zero cancellation between the $v$-weighted regressor channels and $G(q)$.
 
The sum is continuous in $v$, so its minimum $r$ over the unit sphere is positive.
 
Taking $c=\rho^2r$ completes the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $P_k^{-1}=P_0^{-1}+{\mathcal F}_k$ and ${\mathcal F}_k$ is nondecreasing in the Loewner order, $p_k$ is nonincreasing and converges to some $p_\infty\geq0$ on every sample path.

Consider a sample path with $p_\infty>0$.
 
Then $\sigma_k\rightarrow\bar\sigma\stackrel{\triangle}{=}\sigma_0(p_\infty/p_0)^\beta>0$, so there exists $K\geq1$ such that $\sigma_{k-1}^2\geq\bar\sigma^2/2$ for all $k\geq K$.
 
Define $t_j\stackrel{\triangle}{=} K+jN$, ${\mathcal G}_j\stackrel{\triangle}{=}{\mathcal H}_{t_j-1}$, and $\Delta_j\stackrel{\triangle}{=}{\mathcal F}_{t_{j+1}}-{\mathcal F}_{t_j}$.
 
By Proposition~\ref{prop:information_bound} with $k=t_j$, ${\mathbb E}[\Delta_j\mid{\mathcal G}_j]\succeq(c\bar\sigma^2/2)I_{2n}$.
 
Since $\|\phi_i\|^2\leq B$, $\|\Delta_j\|\leq NB$.
 
Hence $D_j\stackrel{\triangle}{=}\Delta_j-{\mathbb E}[\Delta_j\mid{\mathcal G}_j]$ is a bounded martingale difference sequence, and the strong law of large numbers for martingales gives $S_n/n\rightarrow0$ almost surely, where $S_n\stackrel{\triangle}{=}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}D_j$.
 
Then
\begin{align}
    \lambda_{\min}\left(\frac{{\mathcal F}_{t_n}}{n}\right)
        &\geq
        \frac{c\bar\sigma^2}{2}
        -
        \left\|\frac{S_n}{n}\right\|
        -
        \frac{\|{\mathcal F}_{t_0}\|}{n},
    \nonumber
\end{align}
so $\liminf_n\lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_{t_n})/n\geq c\bar\sigma^2/2>0$.
 
Since $\lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_k)$ is nondecreasing, $\lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_k)\rightarrow\infty$ almost surely on this event.
 
This gives $p_k\leq\left(\lambda_{\min}(P_0^{-1})+\lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_k)\right)^{-1}\rightarrow0$, which contradicts $p_\infty>0$.
 
Therefore $p_\infty=0$ almost surely.

It follows that $\sigma_k\rightarrow0$ and $p_k\rightarrow0$ almost surely.
 
Also $\lambda_{\min}({\mathcal F}_k)\geq p_k^{-1}-\lambda_{\max}(P_0^{-1})\rightarrow\infty$, and
\begin{align}
    \frac{\sigma_k}{p_k}
        &=
        \frac{\sigma_0}{p_0^\beta}\,p_k^{\beta-1}
        \rightarrow
        \infty
    \nonumber
\end{align}
since $0<\beta<1$.

Finally, \eqref{eq:rls_theta}--\eqref{eq:rls_P} with $y_k=\phi_k^{\rm T}\theta$ give $\hat\theta_k-\theta=P_kP_0^{-1}(\hat\theta_0-\theta)$, so $\|\hat\theta_k-\theta\|\leq p_k\|P_0^{-1}\|\|\hat\theta_0-\theta\|\rightarrow0$ almost surely.
